description: Splits one polyphonic keyboard stream into two note ranges, each with its own five output jacks and each switchable between passing its channels through and reducing them to one monophonic voice

params.text: Sets the note at and above which an incoming note goes to Zone B, everything below it going to Zone A; -4V to 4V, so eight octaves either side of C4
Arms the module to take its split point from the next note played at the V/Oct input; that note is held back from both zones, and clicking again cancels without a note being played
Switches Zone A to a single monophonic voice whose gate stays high across overlapping notes and drops only when the zone empties; unlit, the zone's channels pass through at their own channel numbers
Switches Zone B to a single monophonic voice whose gate stays high across overlapping notes and drops only when the zone empties; unlit, the zone's channels pass through at their own channel numbers

inputs.text: The polyphonic pitch cable from a MIDI-CV module at 1V per octave; the number of channels on this cable is how many the module reads
The polyphonic gate cable; a channel counts as held while it is at 1V or more
The polyphonic velocity cable, copied to whichever zone each channel falls in
The polyphonic aftertouch cable, copied to whichever zone each channel falls in
The polyphonic retrigger cable; an edge here is what sorts a channel into its zone, and without one a channel is sorted the first time it is found with its gate high

outputs.text: Zone A's pitch at 1V per octave: one channel per input channel in polyphonic mode, or a single channel carrying the priority note in monophonic mode
Zone A's gate: the input gate for the channels in this zone and 0V for the others in polyphonic mode, or one channel at 10V while any note in the zone is held in monophonic mode
Zone A's velocity: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's velocity on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone A's aftertouch: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's aftertouch on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone A's retrigger: the input retrigger for channels in this zone in polyphonic mode, or a 1ms pulse in monophonic mode fired only for a genuinely new key press
Zone B's pitch at 1V per octave: one channel per input channel in polyphonic mode, or a single channel carrying the priority note in monophonic mode
Zone B's gate: the input gate for the channels in this zone and 0V for the others in polyphonic mode, or one channel at 10V while any note in the zone is held in monophonic mode
Zone B's velocity: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's velocity on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone B's aftertouch: per channel in polyphonic mode, or the priority note's aftertouch on one channel in monophonic mode
Zone B's retrigger: the input retrigger for channels in this zone in polyphonic mode, or a 1ms pulse in monophonic mode fired only for a genuinely new key press

notes: the reading at the top shows the split note and its frequency, and right-clicking it opens a field where a note name such as C4 or F#3 can be typed in place of turning the knob
while Learn is armed every output is set to no channels at all, so nothing plays until the split note has been taken
feeding one zone's five outputs into a second Zones module splits that range again, which is how three or more zones are built from one keyboard
in polyphonic mode the pitch, velocity and aftertouch outputs hold their last value on a channel that has left the zone; only the gate and retrigger drop at once
only the first sixteen channels of the input cables are read
menu: Monophonic priority (Zone A): Last note, Highest note, Lowest note — chooses which of the overlapping held notes Zone A plays while it is monophonic
Monophonic priority (Zone B): Last note, Highest note, Lowest note — chooses which of the overlapping held notes Zone B plays while it is monophonic
